title: Cohomology over opens sheafifies to the cohomology sheaf
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space and let $D(\mathcal O_X)$ be the derived category of the abelian category of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. As in [def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image], choose functorially in the complex $K$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules a K-injective resolution $K\to I(K)$ [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. For an open $U\subseteq X$ and $q\in\mathbf Z$ let $H^q(U,-):D(\mathcal O_X)\to\operatorname{Ab}$ be the functor with $H^q(U,K)=H^q(\Gamma(U,I(K)))$ and $H^q(U,f)=H^q(\Gamma(U,I(f)))$ for a morphism of complexes $f$; it is well defined on $D(\mathcal O_X)$ by the argument of [def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image], since $\Gamma(U,-)$ is additive and carries homotopies to homotopies, and for $V\subseteq U$ restriction of sections of $I(K)$ gives restriction maps $H^q(U,K)\to H^q(V,K)$. Then for every object $K$ of $D(\mathcal O_X)$ and every integer $q$, the presheaf $U\mapsto H^q(U,K)$ has sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] canonically isomorphic to the cohomology sheaf $H^q(K)$, naturally in $K$. Consequently, every element of the stalk $H^q(K)_x$ is the germ of some section in $H^q(U,K)$ for an open neighborhood $U$ of $x$, a section whose germ is zero becomes zero after restricting to a smaller neighborhood of $x$, and for a morphism $f:K\to L$ of $D(\mathcal O_X)$ and $s\in H^q(U,K)$ the germ of $H^q(U,f)(s)$ at $x\in U$ is $H^q(f)_x(s_x)$.

proof.text: Put $I^\bullet=I(K)$, with its K-injective resolution $K\to I^\bullet$ as chosen in [def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image]. By the definition in the statement, $H^q(U,K)$ is the degree-$q$ cohomology of the complex of sections $\Gamma(U,I^\bullet)$, with restriction maps induced by those of $I^\bullet$; and since $K\to I^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism, the cohomology sheaf $H^q(K)$ is identified with the cohomology object $\ker(d^q)/\operatorname{im}(d^{q-1})$ of $I^\bullet$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. No restriction of K-injectives to $U$ is needed, since sections over $U$ are taken of the resolution on $X$.

proof.text: For the complex of presheaves of modules $U\mapsto\Gamma(U,I^\bullet)$, kernels, images, and quotients are computed sectionwise. Applying module sheafification to the cycle and boundary presheaves therefore gives the cycle and boundary sheaves of $I^\bullet$: sheafification is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-sheafification-exact]. Since sheafification also commutes with the displayed quotient, the sheafification of $U\mapsto H^q(\Gamma(U,I^\bullet))$ is canonically $\ker(d^q)/\operatorname{im}(d^{q-1})=H^q(K)$. The identification is natural in morphisms of complexes $I^\bullet\to J^\bullet$, which induce compatible maps on the cycle, boundary and cohomology presheaves and sheaves, sheafification being a functor. Applied to $I(f)$ for morphisms of complexes $f$, and since both $K\mapsto(U\mapsto H^q(U,K))^\#$ and $K\mapsto H^q(K)$ are functors on $D(\mathcal O_X)$ factoring through the localization, whose morphisms are composites of images of morphisms of complexes and inverses of images of quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the isomorphism is natural in $K\in D(\mathcal O_X)$.

source.place: Tag 0BKJ, proof, sheafification of cycles and boundaries

proof.text: Let $\theta:\mathcal P\to\mathcal P^\#\cong H^q(K)$ be the sheafification map of $\mathcal P=(U\mapsto H^q(U,K))$ composed with the isomorphism of Step 2. By [lem-weil-pbc-stalk-sheafification-space] $\theta_x$ is an isomorphism, and by [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] $\mathcal P_x$ is the filtered colimit of the groups $H^q(U,K)$ over open neighborhoods $U$ of $x$. Thus every stalk element is a germ of a section on some neighborhood, and a section whose germ is zero restricts to zero on a smaller neighborhood. For $f:K\to L$, naturality of $\theta$ (Step 2) and the definition of the induced map on stalks give $(H^q(U,f)(s))_x=H^q(f)_x(s_x)$. These are the asserted consequences.
